name: Statistics
description: Descriptive statistics, probability distributions and inference for summarizing data and testing hypotheses.

questions.question: What is the median of the data set 3, 7, 9, 15, 100?
questions.explanation: With the values sorted, the middle (3rd of 5) value is 9. 26.8 is the mean.

questions.question: Which measure of center is most affected by extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The mean uses every value's magnitude, so one extreme value can pull it substantially; the median and IQR are robust.

questions.question: A hypothesis test gives p = 0.03. Which interpretation is correct?
options: If the null hypothesis were true, there would be about a 3% chance of observing a result at least as extreme as this one
There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
There is a 97% chance the alternative hypothesis is true
questions.explanation: A p-value is computed assuming the null hypothesis; it is not the probability that either hypothesis is true.

questions.question: Ice cream sales and drowning incidents have a correlation of 0.85. What is the best conclusion?
options: Drowning causes people to buy ice cream
The data must be wrong because the correlation is too high
The variables are strongly positively associated, possibly through a confounder such as hot weather, which does not establish causation
questions.explanation: Correlation measures association, not causation. A lurking variable like temperature can drive both.

questions.question: Test scores are approximately normally distributed with mean 70 and standard deviation 5. About what percentage of scores fall between 60 and 80?
questions.explanation: 60 and 80 are two standard deviations from the mean; by the empirical rule about 95% of values lie within plus or minus 2 SD.

questions.question: What is a Type I error?
options: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis
Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true
Collecting a sample that is too small
questions.explanation: A Type I error is a false positive: rejecting a true null. Its probability is controlled by the significance level alpha. Failing to reject a false null is a Type II error.

practical.title: Compute descriptive statistics
practical.instructions: For the data set 4, 8, 6, 5, 3, 10: compute the mean, the median and the range, and state whether the distribution is roughly symmetric, right-skewed or left-skewed (one sentence). Label each value, e.g. 'mean = ...'.
practical.expected_output: Mean = 6, median = 5.5, range = 7 (10 - 3); because the mean is greater than the median, the data are slightly right (positively) skewed.

rubric.hint: Sort the values (3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10); the median is the average of the two middle values: (5 + 6) / 2 = 5.5.
Mean (6) > median (5.5) suggests a slight right (positive) skew.

tasks.title: Learn descriptive statistics
tasks.description: Complete the Khan Academy units on summarizing quantitative data: mean, median, spread, standard deviation and box plots. Do the practice exercises in each unit.
tasks.completion_criteria: All practice exercises in the summarizing quantitative data unit completed with at least 80% accuracy.

tasks.title: Explore distributions visually
tasks.description: Use Seeing Theory's interactive chapters on basic probability and probability distributions. Change parameters and record how the shape, mean and variance respond.
tasks.completion_criteria: Notes describing the effect of parameter changes for at least three distributions.

tasks.title: Run hypothesis tests on real data
tasks.description: Using a public data set, formulate two hypotheses, run a t-test and a chi-square test in a spreadsheet or Python, and interpret the p-values and confidence intervals in plain language.
tasks.completion_criteria: A short write-up stating hypotheses, test results, p-values, confidence intervals and correct conclusions for both tests.

tasks.title: Design and analyze an A/B test
tasks.description: Design an A/B experiment (e.g. two webpage variants), simulate or collect data, compute the required sample size, analyze the result and discuss Type I/II error risks and practical significance.
tasks.completion_criteria: A report with sample size calculation, test statistic, p-value, confidence interval for the effect, and a recommendation.
